title: HostCapability
description: The host-fulfilled Capability surface. A host capability is declared in `agent.toml` as `[[capabilities.host]]` and referred to from authored source as `Capability("host:<id>")`. The runtime never executes one: it publishes a request, parks the invocation on the durable-event machinery, and settles the node when the embedding host answers. One schema states the whole surface because the three documents are one contract: the declaration set a package publishes, the request a parked node publishes, and the outcome the host returns. Every document carries the same `schema_version`, and the three are mutually exclusive by construction.

input.description: The exact canonical JSON bytes of the authored arguments, as text. The request carries the arguments rather than a reference to them because a host that cannot read the arguments cannot perform the call.

output.description: Present only for `ok`: the exact canonical JSON bytes of the typed output, as text.

receipt_ref.description: The host's own durable record of the effect, carried opaquely into the program's evidence.

message.description: Why a settlement that is not `ok` decided what it decided.

HostCapabilityId.description: The declared id, without the `host:` prefix the authored reference carries. Lowercase dotted segments, so one id reads the same in a manifest, a reference, and a receipt.

HostCapabilityRef.description: The authored reference form: the declared id under the reserved `host:` prefix. No builtin id and no shipped handler directory may occupy this namespace.

HostCapabilityEffect.description: What one call does to the system behind the host. `read` observes; `write` changes. The host decides what the value obliges it to do; APXM carries it verbatim into the request.

HostCapabilityDeclaration.description: One host capability a package declares it needs. The schemas are JSON Schema documents carried verbatim: APXM does not evaluate them, and the host is the party that holds an input against `input_schema` and an output against `output_schema`.

HostCapabilitySet.description: Every host capability one package declares. The minted Capability set a program compiles against is the builtin catalogue united with `host:<id>` for each id declared here; a `host:` reference to anything else is a compile error.

HostCapabilityRequest.description: The request one parked `capability.invoke` node publishes. `capability_request_id` is derived from the invocation and node-execution coordinates, so a re-park after a restart republishes the same id rather than minting a second request for one effect. `authored_permission` is what the program's own source asked for: a request the host may narrow and may never widen, which APXM records and does not broker.

input.description: The exact canonical JSON bytes of the authored arguments, as text. The request carries the arguments rather than a reference to them because a host that cannot read the arguments cannot perform the call.

HostCapabilityRequestId.description: The deterministic identity of one host capability request, derived from the invocation and node-execution coordinates of the node that published it.

HostCapabilityOutcome.description: How one request settled. `ok` carries the output the program receives; `denied` and `failed` settle the node as a typed failure the program observes; `unknown` settles it as an uncertain effect; `cancelled` is recorded by APXM when the request or its invocation was cancelled, and is not a settlement a host may send.

output.description: Present only for `ok`: the exact canonical JSON bytes of the typed output, as text.

receipt_ref.description: The host's own durable record of the effect, carried opaquely into the program's evidence.

message.description: Why a settlement that is not `ok` decided what it decided.
